# What this standard means

Candidate definition: a **standard** is an explicitly maintained set of meanings, rules and evaluation criteria adopted by an identified authority for an identified scope, so people can describe, design and judge things consistently.

This definition is proposed for this collection; it is not an assertion that all standards everywhere have this form. Our collection is standards-development work even while its substantive content remains draft. It differs from a particular operating model, which describes how a particular person or business is arranged and operates.

The standard is named **Manifold**. Business Execution and Operating Model and Execution and Operating Model are historical working titles. The [name and location decision](../../../source-locators.md#source-d0ab2d989102d784) records the current collection and the previous location; the naming change does not alter the accepted scope.

## Interpretation and authority

Owner directions govern the scope recorded in [decisions](../../../source-locators.md#source-877f481c35869210). Assistant proposals, source claims, examples, accepted choices and operational evidence must remain distinguishable. Permission to create files does not accept every candidate statement in them.

Proposed future interpretation rules: distinguish required provisions from recommendations and illustrations; identify the authority and revision to which conformance is claimed; retain exceptions and their approving authority. The normative vocabulary and adoption procedure are not yet agreed.

Open work: EOM-09 in [the ledger](../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a) covers definition, authority, normative wording and adoption. The collection is not a new universal rule imposed on existing projects.

<a id="provision-standing"></a>

## Identifying a provision's standing — proposal

**Standing: proposed for this collection under SEM-026 / EOM-09.** The owner has authorized developing this proposal; its presence here does not record acceptance. The existing scoped decisions below retain their own authority. This proposal concerns interpreting this standard, not deciding whether an external legal or contractual obligation exists.

**Proposed core rule:** Identify the acceptance, material and scope behind a provision before treating it as an adopted part of this standard. Then read what it does: define a meaning, impose a requirement, recommend an approach, permit a choice, or describe a claim or example. Adoption does not turn every sentence into a mandatory instruction.

### Two questions, not more document kinds

1. **What standing does this material have here?** Is there an identifiable acceptance for the relevant material and use, is it a proposal, or is adoption unestablished? Source accounts and examples can support interpretation without becoming adopted requirements. An accepted factual statement can still need evidence; acceptance alone does not establish its truth.
2. **What is the passage saying?** A definition states the local meaning being defined; a requirement sets a condition for the identified subject and scope; a recommendation advises; permission allows an identified choice; a descriptive or predictive claim asserts something that may need evidence. Illustrations show cases under their stated assumptions. These uses can coexist in one document; this is not a mutually exclusive document-kind enum or an adopted glossary replacement.

A heading or nearby standing sentence can identify the section's extent and link its acceptance basis. Retrieve that basis and the applicable material together. Reuse the existing decision record rather than copying authority, dates and revision data into every paragraph or adding mandatory YAML fields. The basis should let the reader recover who accepted what, for which scope, and which text or meaning was accepted. A section, identified proposal, preserved revision or other sufficiently specific reference can provide this; no single new identifier or hashing scheme is selected.

Page-level `status: draft` describes the page as a whole and does not erase explicitly accepted material within it. Conversely, acceptance of one section does not accept its neighbors. The [history decision](../../notes/decisions/history-and-evidence-distinctions.md) identifies six meanings and a representation recommendation; it expressly excludes the remaining time/inference proposals. The [fulfillment decision](../../notes/decisions/conditional-fulfillment-semantics.md) adopts the assessment contract for EOM-03; it does not release the whole standard.

### Patterns and anti-patterns

| Case and distinguishing fact | Warranted reading | Reading to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The history page is draft, while a decision accepts its six named meanings. | Those meanings have scoped acceptance; the page's other proposals retain their stated standing. | Rejecting the meanings because of the page flag, or accepting every neighboring proposal. |
| A hypothetical delivery example stipulates that a client representative can permit staging use. | The permission is a fact supplied for that example. It supports conclusions within the fiction. | Treating the example as a delegation to an actual client representative. |
| A company source says a reviewer must approve a release. | The source reports a rule; its applicability and actual delegation need their own basis. | Treating the quotation as a universal rule of this standard, or as proof that an approval occurred. |
| An adopted recommendation says to use separate representations only when useful. | Preserve its advisory/conditional scope and the accepted meanings. | Turning it into an unconditional requirement for two record types. |
| A report calls an example met under its rubric. | This is a scoped assessment judgment; inspect its criterion, facts and interpretation. | Treating the score as acceptance of the whole standard or proof of actual business success. |

The second and third rows are illustrative situations, not new company facts. The first and fourth use the existing [accepted history scope](../../notes/decisions/history-and-evidence-distinctions.md); the fifth reflects the distinction between assessment and acceptance, without certifying any disputed report grade.

### What to do when standing or meaning is unclear

- If a passage lacks a recoverable acceptance basis, say adoption is **unestablished from the available record**. This does not prove it was rejected or never accepted. Continue work that does not depend on treating it as adopted.
- If a summary, local annotation or page flag conflicts with the recorded accepted scope, expose the mismatch. Do not silently broaden or revoke the acceptance. If competing acceptance records are themselves unclear, retain the conflict for an authority decision; no automatic latest-file-wins rule is proposed.
- A later edit does not by itself establish acceptance of a changed meaning. Editorial clarification need not create a new semantic decision; a substantive change needs its own authorizing basis. When the difference is disputed, make the affected conclusion conditional until the intended scope is settled.
- A quoted imperative, capitalized word, reviewer agreement or saved file does not establish adoption. Once an applicable provision is adopted, its whole wording and linked qualifications determine its force; a requirement need not contain a particular keyword.
- A deliberate local choice needs stated bounds and a chooser or selection rule. An undecided meaning must not be relabeled an application choice merely to avoid resolving it.

[RFC 8174](../../../source-locators.md#source-ea227ca41c6f6096) offers a useful comparison: it makes keyword interpretation explicit while recognizing normative text without those keywords. This proposal does not adopt BCP 14 capitalization, a full normative vocabulary, or IETF governance. Our adoption procedure, exception/delegation rules and final conformance claims remain open.

### Scope of the proposed resolution

This proposal answers how a reader can identify scoped adoption on a mixed-standing page and avoid confusing it with what the statement does. It supplies a reading approach and contrasting examples, not a mandatory metadata schema. SEM-026 / EOM-09 remain open pending the owner's disposition; publishing this draft does not settle every normative term, define a complete adoption procedure or demonstrate reader reliability.

The next connected distinction is [requirement versus prediction](../ontology/concepts/requirement.md): a statement can be selected as a proposed criterion for a design without yet being an adopted obligation, and a prediction about results is not itself a requirement. That term's exact wording remains its owning page's work.

## Linked rules and interpretation guidance

The accepted [problem, context and actor-language requirements](../application/problem-context-and-actor-language.md) govern the opening context, need descriptions and reusable participant wording of documents in this collection. Their [decision](../../notes/decisions/problem-context-and-actor-language.md) records the scoped human direction.

The owner [directed this authoring approach on 2026-09-27](../../notes/decisions/linked-rules-and-interpretation-guidance.md): keep core rules concise and link them to sections here or in other standard documents that explain patterns, anti-patterns, and both resolved and unresolved ambiguity. Those sections support human interpretation and provide contextual examples for a model.

The working implementation is:

1. Give the rule or definition, its scope and its standing. Keep any meaning-changing qualification explicit with the rule or in a clearly identified linked provision; examples must not be the only place a requirement is stated.
2. Link directly to the supporting section. Explain when a pattern applies, the distinction that makes it apply, and the resulting reading or action. Pair it with a plausible misleading reading and explain the difference.
3. Distinguish what has been settled, what an application may choose within stated bounds, what the standard has not decided, and what is unknown about the case. State the consequence for the conclusion or action; do not force a confident classification.
4. Preserve scope, standing, reason, limits and source links when supplying examples as model context. Similarity alone does not establish facts, authority, conformance or an exhaustive list of possibilities.

This is an authoring approach, not a new set of mandatory metadata fields. Its first concrete application is [observation patterns and anti-patterns](../ontology/concepts/occurrences-and-state.md#observation-patterns-and-anti-patterns), linked from the accepted meaning. The [semantic resolution plan](../../../source-locators.md#source-a7fa3c0f38b533d7) sequences the remaining findings and proposes checks. This direction does not decide every open meaning or establish that the model performs better; normative vocabulary and adoption remain EOM-09 work.
